name: Friendly Fire
description: A piece may move only when its destination is defended by another own piece in the resulting position.
ambiguities: Defense is evaluated after the complete move, including en-passant removal, promotion, and auxiliary castling-rook movement. The moving piece does not defend itself.

name: Protected Pawns
description: A pawn may move only when its destination is defended by another own piece in the resulting position.
ambiguities: The restriction applies to the primary pawn mover, including a promoting pawn, and defense is evaluated after the complete move.

name: Rook on the Seventh
description: By the affected player's fifteenth turn, an original or promoted rook must have moved onto the opponent-relative seventh rank.
ambiguities: White's target is rank 7 and Black's is rank 2. On turn 15, only satisfying rook moves are allowed while any exist; failure is checked at the start of turn 16. The observations do not define whether a rook merely occupying the rank without having moved there counts.

name: Rising Water
description: Every ten affected-player turns, one additional rank from that player's home edge becomes underwater; pieces cannot move from or to underwater squares.
ambiguities: Turns are counted separately for the affected player. Water rises from White's rank 1 and Black's rank 8 after each block of ten completed affected-player moves.

name: Queen Disguise
description: The original queen's first move locks it to rook-like or bishop-like geometry for its remaining moves.
ambiguities: Only the original queen is tracked; promoted replacement queens are unrestricted. Identity reconstruction assumes observation from the standard game start.

name: Now Kiss
description: Bishops, knights, and rooks cannot capture until a same-type pair has ended an affected-player turn adjacent; each piece type unlocks permanently and independently.
ambiguities: Adjacency includes orthogonal and diagonal neighbors. Any same-type pair, including promoted pieces, unlocks that type after a completed move. Reconstruction assumes observation from the game start.
